Definition: a (double) stall (for cattle); also a (two-pronged) hook (for flaying animals on)
BiblicalUsage: Hooks and pots share this word, because both are the places where meat is handled. In Ezekiel's temple the hooks, an hand broad, were fastened round about, and upon the tables was the flesh of the offering. The psalm pictures Israel lying among the pots, like sheep in their folds, and yet as the wings of a dove covered with silver.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the temple hooks and the pots both belong to God, because the offering and the flock are both His.
